correctness.rationale: For each zero-one mask S, U^T D_S U is the realized derivative on an open nonempty sign chamber, so the global Lipschitz modulus equals the maximum of their induced infinity norms. A singleton active mask uu^T forces ||u||_infinity ||u||_1=1; equality forces a flat support. The complement mask I-uu^T then has supported row norm 2-2/k, so k<=2. Orthogonality partitions rows into singleton axes or complete orthogonal two-coordinate Hadamard pairs. Every mask for these blocks has infinity norm <=1. All boundaries are handled by continuous piecewise linearity, and the identity chamber gives exact norm one. The checker tests finite examples, not the universal theorem.

value.rationale: The exact all-dimensional rigidity theorem identifies precisely which Euclidean orthant projections preserve coordinatewise perturbation budgets: signed/permuted axes and disjoint Hadamard pairs, with strictly worse stability for every other rotation. This is a structural and motivated robustness classification for orthogonal proximal activation layers, not merely checking a numerical constant or restating Hilbert contractivity. Explicit singleton/complementary mask certificates identify the failure mechanism, and the result is self-contained with no unproved asymptotic extrapolation.
